azure-image-builder.title: Azure VM Image Builder overview – Microsoft Learn
azure-image-builder.notes: Azure VM Image Builder is a fully managed Azure service built on HashiCorp Packer. You submit a configuration that describes the desired image, and the service builds it and distributes it. Builds start from Windows or Linux images in the Azure Marketplace or from your own custom images, and the output can be stored in an Azure Compute Gallery, as a managed image, or as a VHD. The service handles Azure-specific steps such as generalization (Sysprep) and can plug into existing customization scripts and CI/CD pipelines. Typical uses are standardized golden images, baseline security images and images for Azure Virtual Desktop. During a build it creates a staging resource group and temporary build resources, then removes most of them afterwards. Access to artifacts is controlled through managed identities and Azure RBAC, and everything stays in the customer's own subscription. Compute, network and storage are billed at normal Azure rates. Limits include availability in a defined list of regions, restricted Trusted Launch and Confidential VM combinations, no support for moving the image template resource, and no support for Azure Hybrid Benefit.

azure-iot-hub-device-provisioning-servic.title: Overview of Azure IoT Hub Device Provisioning Service – Microsoft Learn
azure-iot-hub-device-provisioning-servic.notes: The Device Provisioning Service (DPS) is a helper service for Azure IoT Hub that enables zero-touch, just-in-time provisioning of devices to the right IoT Hub without manual steps. The manufacturer stores credentials and the DPS endpoint on the device, while enrollments in the cloud define which devices are valid and how they are provisioned. On first boot the device contacts DPS and proves its identity. DPS checks that identity against the enrollment list, assigns the device to a hub, and registers it there. The device then talks to the hub directly, and DPS only becomes involved again for reprovisioning. It supports X.509 and TPM-based attestation, individual and group enrollments, and allocation policies such as lowest latency, evenly weighted and static, plus custom allocation through Azure Functions webhooks. Devices connect over HTTPS, AMQP or MQTT. Typical scenarios are load balancing across hubs, multitenancy, geo-sharding and reprovisioning. Each API call is a billable operation, and there are per-subscription limits, for example on instances, enrollments and linked hubs. Provisioning of nested IoT Edge devices is not supported.

azure-maps.title: Overview for Microsoft Azure Maps – Microsoft Learn
azure-maps.notes: Azure Maps is a collection of geospatial services and SDKs that use current map data to give web and mobile applications geographic context. Its services include Render for vector and raster map tiles and satellite imagery, Search for addresses, places and points of interest, Route for point-to-point, multipoint and vehicle-specific routing, Traffic for flow and incidents, Weather, Geolocation, Timezone and Geofencing. The Web SDK provides interactive maps for JavaScript and TypeScript, and a Power BI visual lets people plot geospatial data without writing code. A Maps preview in Microsoft Fabric supports geovisualization within Real-Time Intelligence. The services are language-agnostic REST APIs that return JSON. Using the service requires an Azure Maps account created in the Azure portal, which provides keys for authentication. The documented limits include unavailability in China and Korea, a required copyright attribution when tiles are used in third-party map controls, and Geolocation returning only a country code for an IP address. Address and location requests are passed to the subprocessor TomTom.

azure-monitor-workbooks.title: Azure Workbooks overview – Azure Monitor – Microsoft Learn
azure-monitor-workbooks.notes: Azure Workbooks provide a flexible canvas in the Azure portal for data analysis and visual reporting. They combine text, log queries, metrics and parameters into interactive reports and can pull from several Azure data sources into one unified view. This makes them suited to open-ended exploration, for example when the relevant metrics for a virtual machine are not yet known. You reach them through Monitor and then Workbooks, or from a Log Analytics workspace page. A gallery lists saved workbooks and public templates published by Microsoft, as well as templates you have deployed yourself. Reports can combine multiple sources, such as composite resource views or cross-resource joins. Access follows the permissions a person has on the resources used in the workbook. The built-in roles Monitoring Reader, Monitoring Contributor and Workbooks Contributor cover reading and saving shared workbooks, and custom roles need the workbooks write permission. Typical uses are investigating VM usage, explaining performance of a new deployment, sharing results of a resizing experiment, and documenting the impact of an outage.

b2b-collaboration.title: What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration? – Microsoft Learn
b2b-collaboration.notes: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration is a feature of Microsoft Entra External ID that lets an organization share its applications and services securely with guests and business partners while keeping control of its own data. Partners sign in with their own credentials, so they need neither Microsoft Entra ID nor their own IT department, and no external accounts, passwords or account synchronization have to be managed. After a guest redeems an invitation or signs up, a user object is created in the directory, typically of type guest. Invitations can be sent from the admin center or through the Microsoft Graph invitation API, and self-service sign-up is possible through user flows with API connectors. Cross-tenant access settings and external collaboration settings control who may be invited, which domains are allowed or blocked, and whether MFA and device claims from other organizations are trusted. Conditional Access policies can be applied to guests, and entitlement management can handle onboarding. B2B collaboration is enabled by default, and when two settings conflict, the more restrictive one applies.

bing-maps.title: Why Bing Maps? – Bing Maps – Microsoft Learn
bing-maps.notes: Bing Maps is a mapping platform for developers that offers a web map control, geocoding, routing and spatial data services. The Microsoft Learn page frames it as an alternative to the Google Maps JavaScript API. The basic map control supports pushpins, polylines, polygons and tile layers, and a modular framework loads extra capabilities such as directions only when they are needed. It offers several map styles, including road, dark, grayscale and high contrast, as well as data visualization options such as data binning layers and a spatial math library. The page highlights use in business intelligence scenarios where the map serves as a backdrop, and in applications with large data volumes or mobile browsers. Licensed customers receive a service-level agreement and round-the-clock phone support for production issues. The most important practical limit is lifecycle: Bing Maps for Enterprise is deprecated, free basic accounts have been discontinued, and enterprise customers can keep using it until 30 June 2028 before REST APIs and SDKs must move to Azure Maps.

bm25.title: BM25 relevance scoring – Azure AI Search – Microsoft Learn
bm25.notes: In Azure AI Search, BM25 is the algorithm that scores results for full-text search. It belongs to the TF-IDF family of retrieval functions but rests on probabilistic information retrieval, and the documentation says it produces more intuitive matches than the older classic algorithm. For each document and query pair it computes a search score that is used to order results, where a higher value means greater relevance and the range is not bounded. The calculation draws on term frequency and inverse document frequency, and index settings let you tune how document length and term frequency affect the score. Only fields marked searchable, or those named in the query, contribute. Services created from July 2020 onward use BM25 permanently, while older services default to the classic similarity unless it is enabled per index. BM25 applies only to full-text queries. Filters, autocomplete, suggestions, wildcard and fuzzy queries are not relevance-ranked, and empty searches return a constant score. Scores can vary slightly between queries or replicas, and sharding can distort ranking in small indexes unless global statistics are requested.

bulkhead-pattern.title: Bulkhead pattern – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
bulkhead-pattern.notes: The Bulkhead pattern separates the elements of an application into isolated pools so that a failure in one element does not take down the rest. The name comes from the partitions in a ship's hull, where a leak floods only one section. It addresses situations in which an overloaded or unresponsive service ties up shared resources, such as connection pools, and causes calls to other services to fail as well. Service instances can be grouped into partitions based on consumer load and availability needs, and consumers can hold a separate connection pool per service they call. Asynchronous services can be isolated through separate queues. Implementations mentioned include processes, thread pools and semaphores, containers and VMs, and resource requests and limits in Kubernetes. Benefits are protection against cascading failure, partial functionality during an outage, and differentiated service quality. The page also lists trade-offs: isolation strength, cost and operational effort must be checked, resource use may be less efficient, the granularity of the partitions must be chosen, and each partition needs monitoring. It recommends combining the pattern with Retry, Circuit Breaker and Throttling.

business-process-flow.title: Business process flows overview – Power Automate – Microsoft Learn
business-process-flow.notes: Business process flows are guided processes that lead users through the steps an organization has defined until a result is reached. They are built from stages and steps, and they appear as a control at the top of a form. Each step corresponds to a column, and a Next Stage button moves a record forward. Steps can be marked required, so a stage cannot be left, and the form cannot be saved, until the data is filled in. The purpose is consistent data entry, less training effort and fewer mistakes, for example in sales or customer service scenarios. A flow can span several tables, with Opportunity to Quote to Order to Invoice as the example, and several flows can be attached to one record, with users switching between them. Flows can be tied to security roles, and their tables can be used for views, charts and dashboards. The page states limits such as a maximum number of active flows per table, stages per process and tables per multi-table process. Business process flows do not provide conditional business logic by themselves, so workflows, business rules or form scripts are needed for that. Enabling the feature on a custom table cannot be undone.

certificate-authority.title: Public Key Infrastructure – Win32 apps – Microsoft Learn
certificate-authority.notes: A public key infrastructure (PKI) is a set of software and hardware elements that lets a trusted third party establish the integrity and ownership of a public key. The certification authority (CA) is that trusted party and acts as the root of trust, offering services that authenticate the identity of people, computers and other entities on a network. The problem it solves is that someone receiving a public key cannot be sure it truly belongs to the claimed sender, since a third party on the channel might have swapped it. The CA binds an identity to a public key by issuing a certificate. To do so it hashes the certificate content, signs that hash with its private key and embeds the signature in the certificate. It publishes its own public key in a self-signed CA certificate, and recipients verify a certificate by decrypting the signature with that public key and comparing hashes. The page lists related components: a registration authority, usually called a subordinate CA in Microsoft PKIs, a certificate database, a certificate store on the local computer and a key archival server. Trust depends on the CA verifying identities correctly, and the page treats this example in simplified form.

circuit-breaker-pattern.title: Circuit Breaker pattern – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
circuit-breaker-pattern.notes: The Circuit Breaker pattern temporarily blocks access to a remote service or resource once failures reach a threshold, so the application stops repeating an operation that is likely to fail. The breaker acts as a proxy that tracks recent failures and decides whether a call goes through or immediately raises an exception. It gives a struggling service time to recover and prevents cascading failures, because blocked calls would otherwise tie up memory, threads and database connections. The proxy is a state machine with three states. In Closed, requests pass through and failures are counted over time. Once the count exceeds the threshold, it switches to Open, where requests fail at once and a timeout timer runs. After the timer expires it moves to Half-Open, where a limited number of requests are allowed; enough consecutive successes return it to Closed, while a failure sends it back to Open. The page contrasts it with Retry, which assumes a later attempt may succeed, and says the two can be combined. Pitfalls include timeouts that are too long, an Open phase that lasts too long, oscillation between states, and a shared breaker blocking healthy parts. It is not suited to local in-memory resources or as a replacement for business-logic exception handling.

cloud-cost-optimization.title: Cost Optimization design principles – Azure Well-Architected Framework – Microsoft Learn
cloud-cost-optimization.notes: In the Azure Well-Architected Framework, cost optimization means making architecture decisions that fit business goals while considering return on investment and financial constraints. The page stresses that a cost-optimized workload is not necessarily a cheap one, because there are trade-offs with security, scalability, resilience and operability. It also says that purely reactive, tactical cuts only lower cost for a short time and that lasting results need prioritization, continuous monitoring and repeatable processes. Five design principles are given. First, develop cost-management discipline with budgets, cost models and clear ownership. Second, design with cost efficiency in mind, using a cost baseline, guardrails and differentiated non-production environments. Third, optimize usage, for example through dynamic scaling and by choosing SKUs whose features are actually used. Fourth, optimize rates through reservations, commitments and cheaper regions for non-production. Fifth, monitor and optimize over time with cost tracking, alerts, architecture reviews and decommissioning of unused or underused resources. Right-sizing means shrinking or removing underused resources or changing the SKU, which reduces waste. Density optimization can weaken security boundaries.

cloud-discovery.title: Cloud app discovery overview – Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps – Microsoft Learn
cloud-discovery.notes: Cloud Discovery in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps compares traffic logs against the product's catalog of cloud apps and scores each app against a large set of risk factors. Its purpose is ongoing visibility into cloud usage, shadow IT and the risk that unsanctioned apps pose to an organization. There are two kinds of reports. Snapshot reports are ad hoc analyses of traffic logs uploaded manually from firewalls and proxies. Continuous reports analyze logs forwarded to the service and can flag unusual behavior through machine-learning anomaly detection or custom policies. Continuous data can arrive through integration with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, a log collector that receives logs over Syslog or FTP, supported secure web gateways, or the Cloud Discovery API. Processing parses each log with a source-specific parser, matches it with the catalog, identifies active users and IP addresses, and produces a risk assessment report. Typical uses are detecting shadow IT and blocking unapproved apps through gateway integrations or block scripts. Limits include that apps missing from the catalog are not detected by default and that newly released log formats may not parse, causing uploads to fail.

computer-using-agent.title: Computer Use – Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry – Microsoft Learn
computer-using-agent.notes: Computer Use is a specialized AI tool, backed by its own model, that carries out tasks by interacting with the user interfaces of computer systems and applications. It interprets what is visible on the screen and acts on it, for example by opening applications, clicking buttons, filling in forms and working through multi-page workflows, and it can adapt when the interface changes. The tool is called through the Responses API and works in a loop. The model returns a computer call with a list of actions such as click, type, scroll, drag, wait or screenshot, the application executes them, and a screenshot is sent back, repeating until no further actions are requested. The model itself does not execute anything, so the calling application is responsible for performing the actions. Access requires registration for the model through a limited-access form and then a deployment. The page defines safety checks for malicious instructions in screenshots, irrelevant domains and sensitive domains, which must be acknowledged before continuing. Its sample is described as experimental, meant for a low-privilege test environment, with a human confirming decisions and no sensitive data exposed to the model.

connected-organizations.title: Manage connected organizations in entitlement management – Microsoft Entra ID Governance – Microsoft Learn
connected-organizations.notes: A connected organization is another organization with which a business relationship exists. For its users to reach your resources, a representation of those users is needed in your directory, which entitlement management can bring in on demand. The purpose is to simplify access for groups of people from specific external organizations and to control which of them may request access packages. Users can be defined in four ways: through another Microsoft Entra directory, through a non-Microsoft directory with SAML or WS-Fed federation, through a shared domain used by email addresses with one-time passcodes, or through Microsoft accounts. One connected organization may cover several directories and domains, and sponsors, who can be internal members or external guests, can act as contacts and approvers. A connected organization is either configured, which is the default for manual creation, or proposed, which is created automatically when a requester has no matching organization and applies only to policies that target it directly. Managing them requires at least the Identity Governance Administrator role, and email one-time passcodes must be enabled for domains without a directory. Domain search needs the full domain name, and domains may be blocked by B2B allow or deny lists.

copilot-search.title: Microsoft Copilot Search – Microsoft Learn
copilot-search.notes: Microsoft Copilot Search is described as an AI-powered universal search designed for enterprises and built into the Microsoft Copilot app as its own Search module. It aims to find relevant results from across the organization quickly, including sources outside Microsoft 365. Search acts as an organizing layer, and users move to Chat when they want to carry out tasks or interact in more depth. Features include unified search across a large catalog of connectors plus custom and partner connectors, semantic understanding of natural-language queries alongside classic keyword matching, and Copilot Answers, which are short AI-generated answers at the top of the results. Administrators can curate answers for acronyms, bookmarks and people. It is available to users with a suitable Copilot license at no additional cost, needs no setup, and supports Entra work or school accounts. Compared with Chat, search is query-based while chat is conversation-based. Compared with free Microsoft Search, it needs a Copilot license and adds semantic search and integration with Copilot Chat answers. Copilot Answers can draw on web content according to the Copilot Chat settings, and several features are still missing in US government clouds.
